text.title: Feedback Management Core Rules
text.summary: Pipeline turning scattered inbound feedback (support, NPS, app-store, sales, social) into ranked product themes via fixed taxonomy, segment-weighted scoring, and close-loop tracking. Feedback sources, categorization taxonomy, six-step processing pipeline, and agent workflow with prompt patterns.

list.item: Support tickets — high volume, high quality (real issues, concrete pain)
In-app feedback widget — medium volume, medium quality (prompted, context-aware)
App store reviews — medium volume, mixed quality (public, harder to follow up)
Sales calls — low volume, high quality (prospect pain, concrete context)
NPS surveys — medium volume, medium quality (prompted, sentiment-reliable)
User interviews — low volume, very high quality (deep intent, behavioral)
Social media — variable volume and quality (unsolicited, harder to categorize)
Type: bug (something broken), request (new capability), enhancement (improve existing), confusion (UX/navigation issue), praise, complaint
Topic: create a product-specific taxonomy — typical: onboarding, core-feature-A, billing, integrations, performance, mobile, other

rule.statement: All feedback channels (support, NPS, app-store, sales, social, in-app widget) MUST normalize into one canonical store with {source, date, user_id, segment, plan_tier, verbatim, classification} per item.
rule.rationale: Multi-store feedback gets re-summarized by each consumer; canonical store enables segment-weighted ranking and de-dup.

rule.statement: Classification MUST use a fixed published taxonomy (<=30 leaves, <=3 levels). New categories require a quarterly taxonomy-review and migration of past items.
rule.rationale: Drift in taxonomy breaks trend lines and makes recurring themes look like new ones.

rule.statement: Theme priority MUST factor segment_ARR × retention_risk × frequency. Raw vote counts alone are forbidden — they over-weight enterprise-customer power users.
rule.rationale: Raw counts privilege the loudest segment; ARR × retention reflects business impact. Weight feedback by ARR or segment, not raw mention count. One enterprise complaint can outweigh 50 free-tier votes. Volume bias: vocal free users post many tickets; at-risk enterprise accounts may post zero. Raw count ranking optimizes for the wrong population.

rule.statement: Items flagged 'will-do' or 'under-consideration' MUST trigger a close-loop email to the requester within 14 days. Items flagged 'won't-do' MUST log a rationale.
rule.rationale: Without close-loop, requesters disengage and the feedback channel decays.

rule.statement: Once per month the PM MUST review the top 10 themes (segment-weighted) and link each to a backlog item, kill decision, or explicit deferral with rationale.
rule.rationale: Themes without monthly disposition pile up; the channel becomes a complaint mailbox, not a decision input.

rule.statement: Triage MUST run daily with a first-touch SLA of 24 hours per item. Batch-triaging only at the monthly review is forbidden.
rule.rationale: The monthly review ranks themes; it cannot classify a backlog that has been rotting for four weeks, and stale items lose the context that made them classifiable.

rule.statement: A theme MUST reach a pre-declared item threshold before it may escalate into discovery or the roadmap; a single verbatim, however senior the requester, cannot become a roadmap item on its own.
rule.rationale: Single-anecdote escalation optimises for the loudest requester and silently overrides the segment-weighted ranking the pipeline exists to compute.

rule.statement: Lock the taxonomy in a versioned file. Treat taxonomy changes as schema migrations: write a migration script and re-tag existing items before applying.
rule.rationale: Taxonomy drift produces categorization inconsistency over time, making trend analysis unreliable. Versioning makes changes auditable and reversible.

rule.statement: Always store the verbatim alongside structured fields. Never lose the original quote.
rule.rationale: Agent rewrites lose intent signals. Original wording reveals tone, context, and use case that structured fields cannot capture.

rule.statement: Auto-responding without human review is a brand risk. Default mode = draft and queue; human approves before send.
rule.rationale: Wrong close-loop email (wrong feature attributed to wrong user, incorrect status) destroys trust harder than no email at all.

rule.statement: Run a quarterly drift audit: sample 50 LLM-categorized items, have a human re-tag, measure agreement rate. If below 80%, retrain or update the prompt.
rule.rationale: LLM categorization drifts as product evolves and language patterns change. Without periodic audit, the taxonomy gradually loses meaning.

rule.statement: Use embedding similarity (cosine >= 0.85) for deduplication, not full-text match. Paraphrases of the same issue are the same issue.
rule.rationale: Naive full-text dedup misses paraphrases. Counting "search is slow" and "search takes forever" as two separate requests undercounts the true signal by half.

rule.statement: Three mandatory human checkpoints: (1) before any outbound message, (2) before promoting feedback cluster to roadmap item, (3) before changing taxonomy.
rule.rationale: Each of these has irreversible effects: sent email cannot be unsent, roadmap items create expectations, taxonomy changes invalidate historical analysis.

rule.statement: If applicability conditions fail (any Skip-If trigger holds — pre-PMF with <5 items/week; compliance-bound feedback awaiting DPA review; sentiment-only loop without commitment to act; single-channel vendor-AI product), the agent MUST skip this methodology and route to the named alternative or to the methodology fallback.
rule.rationale: Mis-applying a methodology outside its preconditions degrades output quality and pollutes downstream artefacts; the explicit skip-rule keeps the routing tree honest.
